# Introduction {#sec-introduction}

Consider the standard infinite-horizon[^1] MDP setup with states $\S$, actions $\A$, rewards $\R$, discount factor $\gamma$, and transition distribution $p: \S \times \A \to \S \times \R$.

This is a post with executable code. See [@Sutton_Barto_2020; @Weng_2018; @Seita_2017; @OpenAI_2018].

[^1]: The proofs for the finite-horizon case are very similar, except with a few additional terms to deal with truncating the trajectories.

$$
\begin{align*}
\E_{s',r \sim  p(\cdot,\cdot\mid s,a)}\left[ r \right] &= \E_{s',r \sim  p(\cdot,\cdot\mid s,a)}\left[ r + \gamma V^\pi(s') - \gamma V^\pi(s') \right] \\
&= Q^\pi(s,a) - \gamma\E_{s',r\sim p(\cdot,\cdot\mid s,a)}\left[ V^\pi(s') \right] \\
&= A^\pi(s,a) + V^\pi(s) - \gamma\E_{s',r\sim p(\cdot,\cdot\mid s,a)}\left[ V^\pi(s') \right].
\end{align*}
$$

# How can we sample more efficiently? {#sec-sample-efficiency}

Many reinforcement learning algorithms are **on-policy**, meaning that to improve the policy, they use rollouts from the current policy. On the other hand, **off-policy** algorithms can use rollouts from any policy to improve the current policy.

Let's consider a hybrid approach, where we sample from the previous policy (denoted $\pi\old$) to update the new policy (denoted $\pi$).

Normally, we optimize $\E_{\pi}\left[V^\pi(s_0)\right]$. However, to use information from $\pi\old$ we can equivilently optimize $\E_{\pi}\left[V^\pi(s_0)\right] - \E_{\pi\old}\left[V^{\pi\old}(s_0)\right]$. In essence, this is the relative improvement instead of simply the global optimum. It's easy to see that the optimal policy will optimize both equations. However, this expression still includes an expectation over $\pi$, which is inneficient for sampling. This raises the question of can we write this expression in terms of exclusively $\pi\old$?

## Surrogate Advantage {#sec-surrogate-advantage}

In reinforcement learning, we seek to optimize the objective $\L(\pi) = \E_\pi\left[V^\pi(s_0)\right]$. How can we write this in terms of $\pi\old$ instead of $\pi$? In this section, we'll only consider the infinite-horizon discounted-reward case, though a similar proof holds for the finite-horizon case (with the addition of a few constant terms to account for the terminating sequences).

Recall that the advantage function is defined in terms of the value function $V^\pi$ and the action-value function $Q^\pi$ as

$$
A^\pi(s, a) = Q^\pi(s, a) - V^\pi(s).
$$

We'll use this identity to rewrite the optimization goal
$$
\begin{align*}
\E_{\pi}\left[ V^{\pi}(s_0) \right] &= \E_{\pi}\left[ \sum_{t = 0}^{\infty} \gamma^tr_t \right] \\
&= \E_{\pi} \left[ \sum_{t = 0}^{\infty} \gamma^tA^{\pi\old}(s_t,a_t) + \gamma^tV^{\pi\old}(s_t) - \gamma^{t+1}\E_{s_{t+1}\sim p(\cdot|s_t,a_t)}\left[ V^{\pi\old}(s_{t+1}) \right] \right] \\
&= \E_{\pi}\left[ \sum_{t = 0}^{\infty}\gamma^t A^{\pi\old}(s_t,a_t) + \sum_{t = 0}^{\infty} \gamma^tV^{\pi\old}(s_t) - \sum_{t = 1}^{\infty} \gamma^tV^{\pi\old}(s_t)  \right] \\
&= \E_{\pi}\left[ V^{\pi\old}(s_0) \right] + \E_{\pi}\left[ \sum_{t = 0}^{\infty} \gamma^tA^{\pi\old}(s_t,a_t) \right].
\end{align*}
$$
We assume here that both $\pi$ and $\pi\old$ share the initial state distribution $\rho_0$. Under that assumption, rearranging terms shows that
$$
\E_{\pi}\left[ V^{\pi}(s_0) \right] - \E_{\pi\old}\left[ V^{\pi\old}(s_0) \right] = \E_{\pi}\left[ \sum_{t = 0}^{\infty} \gamma^tA^{\pi\old}(s_t,a_t) \right].
$$

Rewriting in terms of the state distribution, we see that
$$
\E_\pi \left[ \sum_{t = 0}^{\infty} \gamma^tA^{\pi\old}(s_t,a_t) \right] = \frac{1}{1-\gamma}\E_{\substack{s \sim  d^\pi \\ a \sim  \pi(\cdot\mid s)}}\left[ A^{\pi\old}(s,a) \right].
$$
We see here that we sample from $\pi$ twice: the state $s \sim d^\pi$ and the action $a \sim \pi(\cdot \mid s)$. Since we can calculate the policy $\pi$, we can use importance sampling to instead sample $a \sim \pi\old$:
$$
\frac{1}{1-\gamma}\E_{\substack{s \sim  d^\pi \\ a \sim  \pi\old(\cdot\mid s)}}\left[ \frac{\pi(a \mid s)}{\pi\old(a \mid s)} A^{\pi\old}(s,a) \right].
$$
